headline: AB Enzymes sugar-tolerant enzyme; Amyris buys Oobli; Barry Callebaut Flavourcode; FDA revokes colour solvents
summary: AB Enzymes followed Veron MaxiFresh with a sugar-tolerant anti-staling enzyme for sweet bakery such as brioche and sweet buns, a direct challenge to Puratos softness improvers that should be benchmarked with key industrial accounts.

Amyris is acquiring US sweet-protein start-up Oobli to scale precision-fermented sweet proteins, while Cargill pushed new sugar reduction into bakery, so Patisserie and Belcolade should test Oobli as a supplier and prepare a competitive answer to Cargill.

Barry Callebaut launched its Flavourcode flavour platform and published nine chocolate trends for 2027, and new cocoa extenders appeared from a US gluten-free start-up and a spent-coffee-grounds venture, all partner or competitor signals for Belcolade amid high cocoa costs.

An independent Moldovan-Romanian study found 1-2% Puratos Sapore inactive sourdough raised volume and softness in salt-free wheat bread, ready evidence for sodium-reduction selling alongside the clean-label sourdough launches from Hovis and Toufayan.

Regulatory: FDA revoked authorizations for three cancer-linked solvents used in colour additives, and New York's additive ban awaits a veto decision while FDA prepares to end self-affirmed GRAS, so US coloured icings, glazes and decorations and GRAS-reliant ingredients need auditing now.
